## Commercial workshare

### Recommended offer and customer outcome

Offer **USD 9,600 for 80 delivery hours over 20 productive business days**, covering one existing Budibase workflow from its selected original export through a working target environment, agreed behaviour changes, customer acceptance, production cutover, operator training and continuing ownership. This is a proposed service price. The actual client, archive, application population, assigned people and start date are selected in the original opportunity.

The useful buyer is an agency with an existing client application that its team needs to finish or take into support, or a customer whose prototype needs an accountable production handover. The service should leave the operator able to process its actual requests, decisions and completed work, maintain its connections, recover the application, and make an understood correction. The agency retains its customer relationship and can buy TJLabs as a named delivery workshare. Budibase’s [partner programme](https://budibase.com/partners/) explicitly invites agencies and developers to build client workflows.

The fixed-fee planning envelope is one workflow and one development/production environment pair, using up to two existing supported data sources, 12 existing screens, ten existing tables, five existing automations, four application roles and 20 initially assigned users. Select up to four concrete behaviour changes. If internal data and attachments must move, the authored starting allowance is 10,000 internal rows and 100 MiB of attachments. These are service estimating quantities, not Budibase platform limits or observed customer counts. The entire selected workflow remains the acceptance unit. Actual source discovery determines whether this envelope fits; a larger census receives an explicit priced workshare and date change.

### Work that the customer actually receives

| Delivery phase | Practical result | Platform engineer | Workflow specialist | Lead | Total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1. Source and receiving environment | Select the real request-to-completion flow; inventory its screens, data, automations and roles; select the import route; prepare the target and source/data responsibility map | 12 h | 1 h | 2 h | 15 h |
| 2. Implement and configure | Complete the selected behaviour changes; reconnect the agreed data sources; configure queries, fields, actions and role assignments; deliver the whole flow for customer review | 20 h | 3 h | 2 h | 25 h |
| 3. Customer acceptance and correction | Operate the full workflow with the designated users, resolve the agreed defects, check data transitions and permissions, and rehearse recovery on the selected target | 20 h | 4 h | 2 h | 26 h |
| 4. Cutover and operating handover | Publish the accepted development edition through the actual platform route; complete the live receiving checklist, two operator sessions, correction instructions and continuing responsibilities | 8 h | 4 h | 2 h | 14 h |
| Total | Complete selected customer workflow | **60 h** | **12 h** | **8 h** | **80 h** |

The two operator sessions comprise an administrator/configuration session and an end-to-end business operator session. Provide a short task guide, field and decision definitions, a connection/configuration register with owners, a user/role assignment map, known operating constraints, the actual source and target edition references, and the recovery/correction procedure. Include one complete corrected successor during commissioning. A proposed 14-calendar-day correction window after handover addresses defects against the agreed acceptance; new features and additional applications use the same explicit change process.

An example acceptance course is a requester creating an operational item; a reviewer returning it for correction; an approver assigning it to the correct operating queue; the operator completing the task; and the designated recipient receiving the agreed notification or report. Select the customer’s own entities, fields and decisions before implementation. The receiver then repeats that complete course in the target environment, with the agreed roles and connected data. This delivers the functioning business process behind the export.

### Source route, data and cutover responsibilities

The [complete pinned export/import contract](https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/tree/ce17c2e58d05dd8df4073826106445fa653fc7ea) governs the receiving route. A workspace TAR and a project package have different contents and import behaviour. A workspace update changes development configuration while retaining destination identity and existing-table rows; publication is a separate operation. Project import regenerates identifiers, disables imported automations/apps, clears publication status and requires reconfiguration; it excludes rows and attachments. Select the route that covers the actual source object types. The original agency fixture has 27 revision records including nine tombstones, with six live screen records and three live row records. The expense fixture has 91 records including eight tombstones, with six live screens, five live automations and 30 live rows. Preserve the original records and select repeated document revisions explicitly; raw record counts are separate from the live configuration quantities used to estimate delivery.

Assign the receiving environment and licensed features, connection endpoints, secret re-entry, user membership and role mapping to specific customer/agency owners. Original workspace exports may contain secrets and attachments need their own protection. The implementer uses the existing approved storage and receiving environment for those private inputs. External database migration, a new hosting platform, a custom unsupported connector or plugin, major schema redesign, and an independently staffed emergency response service are separate workshares.

For cutover, retain the current published edition and the selected data backup before changes. Rehearse application restore and the treatment of affected data separately: restoring configuration does not undo external writes or notifications. The runbook states who can publish, when the client’s operating window occurs, which prior edition/data state can be restored, and how the operator deals with a partially completed business transaction. The agency/customer authorizes its production operation through its existing process.

### Payer and internal economics

The contracting payer is the customer or the agency buying the implementation. A proposed 40/40/20 invoice schedule is **USD 3,840 at the agreed start, USD 3,840 when the complete implemented flow is ready for customer acceptance, and USD 1,920 on accepted production handover and receiving**. Net 15 is the initial service proposal; the model also calculates Net 0, 30 and 60. Invoice issuance, contractual due date and expected collection remain different fields.

At authored internal rates of USD 75/h for platform/integration, USD 55/h for workflow/acceptance and USD 100/h for the lead, direct delivery cost is **USD 5,960**. Contribution is **USD 3,640 (37.92%)**. A 10% delivery-cost reserve is USD 596, leaving **USD 3,044 (31.71%)** before general overhead, tax and selling costs. Preserving a 30% contribution after that reserve requires at least USD 9,365.72, so the USD 9,600 anchor has little room for an unpriced material scope increase.

| Customer collection scenario | Peak operating cash requirement | Including USD 596 reserve |
|---|---:|---:|
| Net 0 | USD 0 | USD 596 |
| Net 15 | USD 231 | USD 827 |
| Net 30 | USD 3,788 | USD 4,384 |
| Net 60 | USD 5,960 | USD 6,556 |

These runs pay contributors 14 calendar days after their workdays. Planned collection moves weekend/selected-holiday receipts to the next business day. An additional collection-processing delay is editable. Third-party purchases and platform licences remain customer-owned costs unless the selected contract explicitly assigns them otherwise.

Twenty percent unpriced effort raises direct cost to USD 7,152 and leaves USD 1,852 after the original reserve. Forty percent raises cost to USD 8,344 and leaves USD 660. At Net 30, those cases require USD 4,545.60 and USD 5,303.20 peak cash respectively. Agree the real behaviour changes and source population early; use the original change record to price additional delivery rather than consuming the entire service margin invisibly.

An agency reselling this work at an illustrative USD 12,000 and spending eight account-management hours at USD 75/h retains USD 1,800, or 15%, after paying the USD 9,600 supplier fee. A customer price of USD 14,572 provides approximately 30% agency contribution on those assumptions. These are agency pricing scenarios, not a customer quote or an expected referral commission.

### Capacity and dependency calendar

The model allocates six productive hours per person per business day. Default role labels describe separate capacity pools; they do not identify committed staff. Platform effort peaks at 20 h in a five-day phase, workflow acceptance at four, and lead effort at two. The combined peak is 26 h/week. One suitably qualified person could cover the base hours within a 30-productive-hour week, with the designated customer still performing its acceptance. With 20% extra effort, that one-seat option reaches 31.2 h in the acceptance phase and requires another person or a date change. The calculator identifies the affected dates rather than silently compressing capacity.

The selected start is blank. For a readable calculation only, the default origin is Monday 19 October 2026. Twenty working days finish on 13 November, across 26 calendar days, before any supplied holiday adjustments. Ten business days awaiting customer review plus five awaiting the cutover window move that same 80-hour programme to 4 December, across 47 calendar days. Those waits change the phase dates and linked acceptance collections; they do not automatically create billable work. Additional support or rework during a wait is entered as effort.

### Customer adoption, care and platform cost

Implementation alone needs **eight hours saved per month over 12 months** at an authored USD 100 loaded value per customer hour. Optional care is proposed at **USD 900/month for six productive hours**: four platform/integration, one operating review and one lead hour. Direct care cost is USD 455 and contribution USD 445. Care covers the agreed monthly operating review, selected small corrections and configuration assistance. Emergency/on-call coverage and additional delivery require separately assigned capacity.

With care selected, first-year service expenditure is USD 20,400 and the same break-even threshold is 17 hours/month. The model accepts the customer’s actual current manual effort and actual incremental platform cost. At an illustrative USD 399/month additional licence cost, the threshold becomes 20.99 hours/month. Select care only when the customer’s operating need justifies it.

The current [Budibase pricing page](https://budibase.com/pricing/) displays cloud Pro/Premium/Business monthly equivalents of USD 19/49/299, with annual-billing end-user additions of USD 5 and additional creators at USD 50. Its FAQ applies a 20% uplift for monthly billing. The USD 399 illustration is Business plus 20 end users on that displayed annual basis; the customer’s actual billing frequency, included creators, feature requirements and payment schedule determine its purchase. Premium lists backups/restore and SSO, Business adds environment variables and user groups, and self-hosted open source carries separate infrastructure/operating responsibilities. Record the selected plan instead of treating an exported archive as a licence entitlement.

### Service revenue and referral revenue

The [current introducer terms](https://budibase.com/partner-terms/) separate professional services from licence commission. Eligibility requires Budibase-approved account registration and the appointment’s commission rate. The published minimum qualifying initial subscription net revenue is USD 7,200, with the initial period limited to 12 months; implementation/training fees and renewals are excluded. Commission follows Budibase’s cleared receipts and is due by the end of the month after that quarter. A registered account’s professional-service opportunity has stated support/capability exceptions.

Therefore this model funds delivery from its service invoices and defaults referral cash to zero. A separate, explicitly confirmed scenario can enter an eligible amount, rate and original provider receipts. The demonstration USD 12,000 qualifying receipt on 20 October at an authored 10% yields USD 1,200 due 31 January 2027; the 10% is illustrative, not a published entitlement. The USD 9,600 engineering fee itself does not satisfy the subscription threshold.

### Editable model and operator integration

The pure `calculateBudibaseWorkshare(input)` function returns the complete input, source scope basis, role allocations, phase dates, invoices, individual work/cost obligations, daily cash, capacity conflicts, care economics, customer break-even, agency resale economics and a separate referral schedule. `budibaseScenarios(input)` returns the 12 collection/effort comparisons. Its named scenario inputs preserve the longer review/cutover wait, optional care/platform cost, shared-seat capacity and agency/referral examples. Daily cash covers commissioning invoices and contributor payments, plus separately selected eligible referral receipts; optional care is reported as monthly unit economics and customer adoption expenditure. Invoice cents use a nonnegative largest-remainder allocation. If an included referral payment date precedes the first workday, the cash ledger starts at that earlier date while the delivery calendar retains its selected start.

Store the selected inputs and calculated result with the original customer implementation plan. The actual export inventory informs the selected scope and role/configuration work; commercial changes preserve their original reasons and accepted dates. The complete source and base result below allow another operator to reproduce or adjust the whole programme.

# Budibase commissioning programme

## Customer outcome

Receive an existing low-code application, agree and perform its required implementation changes, configure its target services and roles, operate the real customer process with an independent reviewer, and deliver a complete source and operating handover. The browser app and Node CLI share the same commissioning engine. They do not alter or publish a Budibase installation automatically.

The original archives and all revision records remain in the saved project. The selected live configuration determines the displayed inventory and suggested operating cases. Later corrections add new observations and plans; accepted editions keep the exact operating results originally accepted.

## Open the programme

Open index.html in a current desktop or mobile browser. The app is self-contained and makes no network requests. Browser storage uses IndexedDB. Keep downloaded projects in approved customer storage and download a full project after significant work. Browser storage alone is not a backup.

Select New project and enter the actual customer or workstream. Receive the original export, or use an included official template to learn the flow. The three official sources are copied from Budibase commit ce17c2e58d05dd8df4073826106445fa653fc7ea. Sample data remains labelled as sample data; it is never presented as a deployed customer workflow.

The archive password is used for the current in-memory read and cleared from the input. Source exports themselves may contain confidential data or configuration; protect all project/handover files accordingly.

## Original source routes

Current workspace exports are gzip-compressed TAR archives containing root db.txt, optional global.txt and original attachment/object-store files. The database is newline-delimited PouchDB JSON. Complete original members and source bytes are retained. Password-protected regular files use the pinned Budibase encryption format; the programme derives the key locally and decrypts only for inspection.

Project packages are a different archive contract. The root manifest declares formatVersion 1 and artifactType project. The programme reads project.json, dependency-index.json and the complete supported docs directory. Budibase's native project importer creates new destination IDs and changes activation/default state; inspect and operate that actual destination before acceptance.

The included agency-client-portal and expense-approval TARs are legacy catalogue templates. Their database is nested under template-name/db/dump.txt. The programme's Extract original legacy database button downloads that original plaintext database unchanged for the native legacy import route. Uploading the catalogue TAR as if it were a current root-db.txt workspace archive is incorrect.

The Old App plaintext source is the complete official 8,139-byte legacy import fixture. Native migration is performed by the selected Budibase installation. Retain the original export and compare its resulting live configuration and required records.

Archive limits are 64 MiB compressed, 256 MiB expanded, 20,000 members and 24 MiB for the inspected database. TAR names and checksums are checked, and no archive member is executed or extracted to the filesystem by the core inspector. Use a separately provisioned native receiver for larger projects and keep the same complete source identity.

## Revision and scope census

Original PouchDB exports can include multiple records for an ID and tombstones. The programme retains all records, removes known ancestor revisions from the selectable leaf set and chooses a deterministic live inspection view. Multiple retained leaves remain an explicit review decision. The destination's native database is authoritative for its imported result.

Agency sample: 27 original records, 25 unique document IDs, nine selected tombstones and 16 live documents. There are six live screens, two tables and three rows. Expense sample: 91 original records, eight tombstones and 83 live documents; six screens, five automations, four tables and 30 rows.

Configuration comparison uses original document IDs and content, ignoring revision counters and timestamps. It reports additions, removals and changed configuration. Comparing separate workspace identities is explicitly labelled.

## Plan the implementation

Enter the actual installation, destination workspace/new name, native import route, target version, implementation operator and acceptance reviewer. Define the customer business outcome, agreed implementation changes and the recovery procedure, including reconciliation of work performed after the selected backup.

Assign each explicit connector and custom role to an accountable owner. Record the destination/configuration decision and a reference to credentials in the approved secret store. Resolve each source finding with the actual target decision.

Edit the operating-case list for the agreed customer process. Preserve unique IDs and clear expected business results. Suggested cases include complete source receiving, business-data results, a complete correction, independent operator receiving and recovery. Each live screen/query/automation adds its actual operating case.

Save the plan. A new plan is immutable and pinned to one source. Use the retained-plan selector to reopen an earlier plan or prepare a successor from the selected capture. Source/version changes require a corresponding plan.

## Operate and accept

Perform the native import and implementation work in the approved Budibase destination. Configure services and roles. Operate the real records, screens and automations as the intended role. Record the actual operator, outcome, detail and run/ticket/document reference in the programme.

A failed or needs-work result prevents issuing a new accepted edition until a later passing result exists for that same case and saved plan. Correct the implementation, rerun the original process and record the actual replacement result. Earlier outcomes remain visible in project history.

Issue an edition only after all selected cases pass and the named reviewer accepts the result. A later failed observation does not rewrite an already-issued edition's historical report.

## Hand over and independently receive

Select the exact accepted edition and download both its operator report and Complete handover. The complete handover contains every original capture, all plans and observations, the selected original edition and the original source index. Save the full project for continued internal work.

Open the handover in a second browser profile or use CLI receive in a new file. The receiver validates source bytes, plan digests, original accepted case references and the selected report. It can download each original archive again. In the same browser, a received extension is adopted only when the saved earlier source, plans, observations, editions, events and request history are preserved. Older handovers reopen their selected edition while retaining newer local work. Divergent histories require explicit reconciliation using separately saved copies.

Publishing the native Budibase app is a separate target action after configuration and receiving. Existing-workspace import preserves destination identity and existing-table rows according to the pinned importer; it must not be treated as a blind destructive restore.

## Commercial programme

The Commercial section edits the full input model, then calculates staffing, milestone invoices, collection timing, daily cash, capacity, care and referral scenarios. Default offer: USD 9,600, 80 hours, 20 business days. Scope covers implementation, independent receiving, adoption and complete handover.

The internal model includes costs, reserve and sensitivity. A saved commissioning plan carries only the customer fee/currency/scope selection; internal cost and margin inputs are kept in the separate commercial calculation. Platform subscriptions remain separate. Referral income is zero by default and must satisfy the actual appointment and qualifying subscription terms.

Read commercial/BUDIBASE_COMMERCIAL_WORKSHARE.md for the full workshare and assumptions.

## Inspect the delivered application and every attachment

The producing operator opens and looks at the exact outgoing application and all its attachments before presenting that edition as ready. Operate the important controls at the actual screenshare width and at a narrow phone width. View the real screen or the actual screenshots; saving image files alone does not complete inspection. Inspect populated, empty, busy and error states, each download and independent reopening. Repair unreadable, clipped, overflowing, cramped, unstyled or broken output in this same product. Keep the industrial interface: readable tables, clear hierarchy, consistent spacing and typography, restrained controls and useful labels. Code checks and successful HTTP responses support this course; they do not replace looking at it.

Use a separate receiving browser profile so the existing customer project remains intact. Record the exact source commit or complete file SHA, browser, viewport and original project identity. Use 1440 × 1000 and 390 × 844 for the reference desktop and phone course, adjusting the desktop view to the actual presentation window.

1. Open the complete standalone index.html. Look at the loading notice until the original modules and saved-project list have opened. Inspect the empty-project view, the five section links, visible labels, keyboard focus, wrapping and table scrolling. Create the named receiving project using the visible name field.
2. Receive the selected complete original export. In the reference source course, open the official legacy workspace and retain its original 8,139-byte source. Look at the populated inventory, original record/tombstone counts, source identity and expanded inventory. Filter to a known original ID, then to no matches and clear the filter. Download the original and complete inventory, open both, and compare the original file's bytes with the selected capture.
3. Open each original official template selected for the course. Inspect its full source/legacy-format notice and inventory, then operate configuration comparison and capture selection. The agency and expense templates remain separate original sources. Open their extracted legacy databases and retain their source binding.
4. Prepare the actual source-receiving plan, fill its target, owners, findings and operating cases, save two plan alternatives and reopen the first. Inspect the complete form and plan selection at both widths. Record only the outcome actually performed: for the reference local source course this is the exact original byte transfer and independent reopening. The selected Budibase installation supplies any application-deployment outcome.
5. On the receiving copy, inspect a needs-work or failed observation and its visible readiness result, correct the same actual task, and record its later passing result. Use the actual accepting operator and decision to issue that source-receiving edition. Confirm the selected edition, report and original result history remain readable.
6. Exercise an invalid source or malformed project in the separate receiving profile. Look at the visible error and confirm the current original project and selected edition survive. Return to the valid workflow. During a real large-source read or calculation, observe the busy controls and restored availability.
7. Calculate the full commercial programme from its explicit input. Inspect the displayed fee, staffing and collection summary, then expand the full result and download the complete JSON. Open that JSON and reconcile its input, milestone amounts and cash results with the selected view. Original proposed economics remain separate from actual customer outcomes.
8. Use Save full project, Download operator report, Download complete handover, Download operating guide and Download programme. Open every emitted attachment in its normal viewer. Inspect the report content, full history and selected edition; extract the programme ZIP and inspect its opening HTML, source, fixtures, licences, guides and calculation files. JSON and source attachments must be readable in an appropriate text/data viewer, with original fields and complete bytes intact.
9. Close the original tab, reopen the saved project, and verify the original capture, selected plan, observation history and accepted edition. In a fresh browser profile, open the extracted programme's index.html and receive the complete handover. Repeat source download and a complete project export. Inspect desktop and phone views of this received copy and compare its original IDs, revisions, edition and source digests with the delivered record.

Keep the actual viewed screenshots and concise observed corrections with the original receiving result. When another equipped operator renders the programme, return its exact-version images to the producing operator for direct inspection and integrate any repairs before the final delivery. Preserve the existing operation, complete working project and source history throughout this course. If a delivery also contains audio or video, play the complete final media and inspect its picture, timing, speech and natural voice quality.

## Source and maintenance

Download programme exports every source file, the standalone app, official fixtures, Node CLI, operating guide and commercial model. Node build.mjs rebuilds index.html from the complete source packet using builtin gzip. No dependency installation is required for the normal CLI or build.

The original upstream contract is:
https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/tree/ce17c2e58d05dd8df4073826106445fa653fc7ea

Official product documentation:
https://docs.budibase.com/docs/export-and-import-apps
https://budibase.com/partners/
https://budibase.com/partner-terms/

Budibase fixture licensing is retained in UPSTREAM_LICENSE.txt. The commissioning implementation is separate product code; the original fixtures retain upstream notices.

# Budibase commissioning command line

This command line operates the same complete commissioning core as the browser.
It retains the original Budibase export, source inspection, plans, actual operating
observations, issued editions, request receipts and complete customer handovers.

## Install and open

Use Node.js 22 or newer on Linux or another POSIX filesystem that supports hard
links, atomic rename and directory synchronization. Place cli.mjs, core.mjs,
CLI_GUIDE.md and UPSTREAM_LICENSE.txt together. They use Node built-ins and need
no package installation. The upstream source contract is pinned in the core.

Choose an existing private working directory with room for the complete source,
project and recovery request files. Project and request files are private mode
0600; the lease directory is 0700. The project file is a complete JSON envelope.
The original core project can be exported separately with open --out.

    mkdir -m 700 /private/budibase-job
    node cli.mjs create --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --id client-workflow --name "Customer workflow" --request /private/budibase-job/create.request.json
    node cli.mjs open --project /private/budibase-job/project.json

A create operation requires a new project path. Repeating its exact request opens
that same created project, including later saved work. An unrelated existing
project is preserved. All commands print structured JSON; failures return exit 1
and a concrete error. Read commands do not acquire the writing lease.

## Receive the exact original export

    node cli.mjs capture --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --source /private/original-workspace.tar.gz --request /private/budibase-job/capture.request.json

The capture retains complete original bytes, SHA-256, the member inventory, original
document revision records, source findings and its selected resource inventory.
The core accepts native gzip TAR workspace exports, project packages, complete
legacy catalogue templates and the supported plaintext PouchDB NDJSON format.
It preserves unknown members in the unchanged original archive.

For encrypted native members, put the exact password in a separate private UTF-8
file and add --password-file /private/export-password.txt. One final newline is
removed. The password is read only to inspect the source and is omitted from the
retained request and project. Its file locator appears in the private request
binding. The decoder uses the pinned native PBKDF2-SHA512, AES-256-CTR and inner
gzip contract. Original encrypted archive bytes remain encrypted in the capture;
the resulting inspection contains configuration facts and field names.

The core enforces a 64 MiB original export, 256 MiB expanded TAR, 20,000 members
and 24 MiB database-document inspection limit. Complete projects and handovers
are JSON and therefore require memory for their whole histories and source bytes.
Choose a receiving machine appropriate for the actual project. Original source
files and customer configuration stay in the selected private directory.

Open reports every capture with its source identity and actual document counts.
To return to an earlier capture:

    node cli.mjs select --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --capture capture-ORIGINAL_ID --request /private/budibase-job/select.request.json

## Prepare the complete commissioning plan

    node cli.mjs plan-template --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --out /private/budibase-job/plan.json

Edit that complete JSON. It includes the actual source's connectors and roles,
all source findings, and suggested source/data/workflow/screen/query/automation/
handover/recovery cases. Assign each connector or role's owner and decision;
resolve every retained finding with its actual decision. Choose the real receiving
installation, destination workspace, target Budibase version, operator and reviewer.
Record the customer outcome, implementation changes and the recovery plan.

Supported target modes are new-workspace, update-existing and project-import.
The core binds project exports to project-import and complete workspace exports
to a workspace route. Native existing-workspace import preserves existing-table
rows and the destination identity; project import remaps resource IDs and imports
applications and automations disabled. Native import, destination configuration,
data reconciliation and publication are performed through the selected Budibase
installation. Record their results in the corresponding operating cases.

    node cli.mjs plan --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --input /private/budibase-job/plan.json --expect 1 --request /private/budibase-job/plan.request.json

Reopen an earlier saved plan and its corresponding retained source:

    node cli.mjs plan-select --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --plan plan-1 --request /private/budibase-job/plan-select.request.json

The selected source is fixed into the saved plan. --expect is an optional explicit
project revision. If omitted on a new request, the command uses the current
revision while holding its lease. A stale explicitly selected revision is rejected
before project replacement.

The commercial field can hold the complete selected workshare input and calculated
outcome from the commissioned model. Keep its quantities and funding choices tied
to the source and agreed work. Saved plan history remains immutable.

## Record actual outcomes and issue the handover

Write an observation JSON for one saved case:

    {
      "caseId": "source",
      "outcome": "passed",
      "actor": "Named receiving operator",
      "detail": "Describe the actual source and destination result, including any discrepancy.",
      "reference": "The retained original operating record or artifact identity"
    }

Use passed, failed or needs-work. Each observation is appended and tied to the
exact plan digest. Use a distinct request file for a new observation.

    node cli.mjs observe --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --input /private/budibase-job/observation.json --request /private/budibase-job/observation-1.request.json
    node cli.mjs ready --project /private/budibase-job/project.json

ready returns every case and its latest observation, including missing or failing
cases. Corrective work is recorded with another observation. Changing the plan
creates a new plan digest and requires its own operating outcomes.

After the cases are complete, prepare acceptance JSON:

    {
      "acceptedBy": "Named accepting operator",
      "acceptance": "The actual scope and accepting decision"
    }

    node cli.mjs issue --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --input /private/budibase-job/acceptance.json --request /private/budibase-job/issue.request.json
    node cli.mjs handover --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --out /private/budibase-job/Customer_Complete_Handover.json

The handover contains the entire core project, every original capture's bytes,
saved plans, observations, edition history, the selected operator report, all
source digests and the complete CLI/core/guide/license files. An explicit earlier
edition can be selected with --edition edition-N; the full project history travels
with it. Use a new output path for a changed edition or source programme.
An already existing byte-identical output is recognized without replacement;
different output bytes are preserved and reported.

## Independent receiving and original-source downloads

    node cli.mjs receive --project /private/customer-copy/project.json --input /private/budibase-job/Customer_Complete_Handover.json --request /private/customer-copy/receive.request.json
    node cli.mjs open --project /private/customer-copy/project.json
    node cli.mjs source --project /private/customer-copy/project.json --capture capture-ORIGINAL_ID --out /private/customer-copy/original-workspace.tar.gz

Create the private customer-copy directory first. receive also accepts a complete plain core project or an original CLI project file, so an unfinished operating project can be recovered at a new independent path. The input byte identity and previous CLI origin are retained in the new origin. Receiving checks the complete
project, every retained original source, saved plan digests and the selected
operator report before creating the new independent project. The same native
capture and edition identities survive receiving. A new local plan or observation
then uses an original new request against that project's current revision.

source writes the complete raw original archive or plaintext export and verifies
its exact bytes and SHA-256. The caller chooses the output path; the tool returns
the original filename and capture identity. It never extracts archive paths into
the filesystem. Use the original Budibase import route described in the report
when operating the selected destination.

For interchange with the browser core:

    node cli.mjs open --project /private/customer-copy/project.json --out /private/customer-copy/core-project.json

This exports the complete core project as plain JSON. Complete issued handovers
use the same tjlabs.budibase-complete-handover/v1 format consumed by core.receive.
The CLI's additional programme files do not replace the native project or report.

Compare two retained original source editions:

    node cli.mjs compare --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --before capture-EARLIER --after capture-LATER --out /private/budibase-job/Source_Changes.json

The comparison retains both capture IDs and identifies added, changed and removed
resources. Data and external service behavior remain part of the actual operating
course.

## Resume exactly after interruption

The first attempt saves a complete immutable request file before applying its
mutation. That file contains the original operation ID, expected revision,
timestamp and full input. A capture request also includes the original source bytes
and inspection, so later recovery needs neither the source path nor the password.

    node cli.mjs resume --request /private/budibase-job/capture.request.json

The same original command with exactly the same arguments also reuses its request.
It deliberately replays the bytes already recorded there, even if an input file
at that name was subsequently edited. Use a new request file for changed input.
Request files are separate from project and lease-history paths.

If the project save completed but its response was lost, the core's request receipt
returns that original result without another revision. If the request was saved
before a failed project write, resume performs the same operation. A saved stale
request retains its original expectation and can be inspected; new intent belongs
in a new request. Original requests and their input files should remain with the
private operating directory until the handover and recovery copy are received.

Every project replacement is a fully written, synchronized private sibling file
published by atomic rename, after comparing the original complete file SHA while
holding the same project lease. Initial files and all exports use create-only hard
link publication. Complete existing files are never truncated in place. If a process stops between publishing an initial project link and removing its private temporary name, the next leased continuation recognizes only its matching same-parent UUID temporary links, verifies inode, device, owner and private mode, removes those redundant links and synchronizes the parent. Unrelated hard-link aliases remain preserved. Replaying an already received result also synchronizes the project directory to complete an interrupted publication.

## Original writing lease

The project has an adjacent .leases directory. Each operation publishes a complete
numbered lease by exclusive hard link and later writes its immutable release.
Generations are never reused or deleted. Concurrent writers compete for the same
next generation; only one can publish it. This avoids deleting another process's
new lock while recovering an old one. Canonical real parent paths ensure that
symlink aliases use the same project lease.

    node cli.mjs lease --project /private/budibase-job/project.json

If a process was interrupted before release, inspect its retained token, PID,
process start identity, host, boot and PID namespace. Once the original process has
ended, release that exact generation on its original host:

    node cli.mjs lease-release --project /private/budibase-job/project.json --token ORIGINAL_TOKEN
    node cli.mjs resume --request /private/budibase-job/capture.request.json

lease-release verifies that the original process ended in the retained host, boot and PID namespace, using its PID and process-start identity. Different boot identities remain unverified rather than being treated as proof of a remote process ending. A running or unverified remote process keeps its
original lease. Receiving a complete handover, plain core project or original CLI project file at a fresh project path is the
independent operator transfer; it leaves the original operation history intact.

## Complete command reference

| Command | Required inputs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create | project, id, name, request | New project with durable creation origin |
| open | project; optional out | Complete summary or plain core project |
| capture | project, source, request; optional password-file, expect | Exact source and inspection |
| select | project, capture, request; optional expect | Select an earlier retained capture |
| plan-template | project; optional out | Complete editable source-linked plan |
| plan | project, input, request; optional expect | Immutable saved plan |
| plan-select | project, plan, request; optional expect | Select an earlier plan and its source |
| observe | project, input, request; optional expect | Original plan-bound observation |
| ready | project | Full current case outcomes |
| issue | project, input, request; optional expect | Accepted edition after all cases pass |
| compare | project, before, after; optional out | Complete resource change projection |
| handover | project, out; optional edition | Whole customer project and programme |
| receive | project, input, request | Independent complete project creation |
| source | project, out; optional capture | Exact original source bytes |
| resume | request | Same original operation and receipt |
| lease | project | Current generation and process status |
| lease-release | project, token | Release a confirmed ended original process |

All inputs in the table are named --options. Quoted strings retain spaces. The
command line performs local commissioning record and file operations; the selected
Budibase installation remains the native application execution and publishing
surface.

## Receive the rendered product and attachments

After the complete CLI course, follow the full desktop/phone and attachment procedure in OPERATING_GUIDE.md, section “Inspect the delivered application and every attachment.” Open the exact rebuilt index.html, import the complete original core project or accepted handover, operate capture/plan/result/edition/commercial controls, view the real rendered output and every exported attachment, then reopen the extracted programme and original handover in a fresh browser profile. Use the existing operation and source identities. A completed CLI response does not by itself complete the rendered application receiving. Retain actual viewed images and repair concrete presentation or control defects in this same delivery.

# Budibase commissioning

An offline workspace for receiving an existing Budibase application, planning its implementation, recording actual operating outcomes, and handing the complete project to another operator.

The browser and Node command line share one core. The workspace retains original exports and document revisions, immutable plans, case observations, accepted editions, and byte-for-byte source downloads. It distinguishes current workspace archives, project packages and legacy catalogue templates.

## Start

Open [index.html](index.html) in a current browser. No account, server or dependency installation is required for the offline application.

For the command line, use Node.js 22 or newer on a POSIX filesystem:

```sh
node cli.mjs help
mkdir -m 700 ./customer-work
node cli.mjs create --project ./customer-work/project.json --id customer-workflow --name "Customer workflow" --request ./customer-work/create.request.json
node cli.mjs capture --project ./customer-work/project.json --source /absolute/original-export.tar.gz --request ./customer-work/capture.request.json
node cli.mjs plan-template --project ./customer-work/project.json --out ./customer-work/plan.json
```

Edit the plan for the actual target, implementation scope, service and role owners, independent reviewer and operating cases. Perform the native import and application work in the selected Budibase installation, then record the actual results. The programme retains the commissioning record; the installation performs native execution and publication.

- [Operating guide](OPERATING_GUIDE.md): complete source-to-acceptance and independent receiving workflow.
- [CLI guide](CLI_GUIDE.md): all commands, original requests, atomic project publication, and interrupted-operation recovery.
- [Commercial programme](commercial/BUDIBASE_COMMERCIAL_WORKSHARE.md): editable scope, staffing, invoice, cash, capacity and adoption model.
- [Source provenance](SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json): exact upstream commit and original fixture identities.

## Build and complete handover

```sh
node build.mjs
```

The builder reads the actual complete source files named by source-packet.json and rebuilds index.html with their compressed contents. The app's Download programme action exports that full editable source and the standalone app. Complete customer handovers retain every original capture, saved plan, observation and edition; the CLI includes its complete receiving programme.

The two compressed official examples are retained as exact base64 files under fixtures/. The browser decodes them directly. Their original compressed byte counts and SHA-256 values are in SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json.

## Review and limitations

The shared engine and original official examples were exercised in V8, and the browser, commercial model and CLI received independent source review. Native deployment outcomes and customer case results are entered by the commissioned operators.

Needs expert review: confirm the chosen Budibase version and import effects, actual role and connector configuration, customer acceptance, and commercial assumptions for the selected engagement. The default fees, costs and role capacities are editable planning examples.

## Licence

The commissioning implementation uses the repository's MIT licence, copied into [LICENSE](LICENSE). Original Budibase examples retain their upstream licence and provenance. See [THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md) and [UPSTREAM_LICENSE.txt](UPSTREAM_LICENSE.txt).

## Complete receiving

The operating guide includes the actual desktop, phone, all-attachment and cold-reopen receiving course. Open and inspect the exact outgoing programme, operate its controls, view its real screenshots and open every emitted attachment before presenting that edition as ready. Preserve the original source/project identities and integrate concrete repairs in the same product.
